sections.normalized_html: The domain of the function [MATH: f(x) = \dfrac{5}{2x-a}+3] is [MATH: (-\infty,3) \cup (3 ,+\infty).] What is the value of [MATH: a?]
sections.readable_text: The domain of the function [MATH: f(x) = \dfrac{5}{2x-a}+3] is [MATH: (-\infty,3) \cup (3 ,+\infty).] What is the value of [MATH: a?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
A reciprocal function is defined for all values of [MATH: x] except for those that make the denominator zero. So, to find the domain, we must exclude all values that make the denominator zero.

Setting the denominator equal to zero and solving, we get [MATH: 2x − a|= 0; 2x|= a; x|= (a)/(2).]

So, the point that must be excluded from the domain is [MATH: x = \dfrac{a}{2}.]

On the other hand, we can see that [MATH: x=3] is excluded from the domain. Equating this to [MATH: \dfrac{a}{2},] we get

[MATH: (a)/(2)|= 3; a|= 6.]

Therefore, the range of [MATH: y = f(x)] is
